title: Stanislav Petrov and the 1983 nuclear false alarm
sources: Wikipedia: 1983 Soviet nuclear false alarm incident — 26 September 1983; Oko reported one ICBM from the US, then four more; shortly after midnight; Serpukhov-15 bunker near Moscow; launch-on-warning doctrine; Petrov reasoned a real first strike would be hundreds of missiles; no missiles arrived; cause: sunlight on high-altitude clouds and the satellites' Molniya orbits

Wikipedia: Stanislav Petrov — duty officer; 'often credited as having saved the world'; no reward; 'My late wife for 10 years knew nothing about it. "So what did you do?" she asked me. "Nothing. I did nothing."'

post.facebook:
On this day in 1983, a Soviet officer may have saved the world — by doing nothing.

Just after midnight on 26 September, Lieutenant Colonel Stanislav Petrov was on duty at the early-warning bunker near Moscow when the computers reported an American missile on its way. Then four more.

Protocol said report it, at a moment when the Soviet system was primed to strike back. But Petrov reasoned that a real American attack would mean hundreds of missiles, not five. He called it a false alarm and waited. No missiles came: the satellites had mistaken sunlight on high clouds for rocket launches.

He was never rewarded. For ten years his wife knew nothing about it. When she finally asked what he had done, he told her: "Nothing. I did nothing."
